en.title: ea
en.summary: This is the letter L317 from the vowel-consonant groups.

sections.title: Sound of ea
paragraphs: The letters ea have no single name. Their main sound is the long vowel /iː/, as heard in (eat) /iːt/, which means to take food. Together these letters make three distinct vowel sounds across English words.

sections.title: How to say ea
paragraphs: For the first sound, spread your lips wide and raise your tongue high near the roof. For the second sound, relax your lips and open your mouth a little wider. For the third sound, slide smoothly from a mid vowel into a high front vowel. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz continuously for each one.

sections.title: Spelling of ea
paragraphs: Most commonly, these letters make the long sound /iː/, as in (meat) /miːt/. Before certain consonants like d, th, or l, they often make the short sound /ɛ/, as in (bread) /brɛd/. In a few special words, they sound like /eɪ/, as in (great) /ɡreɪt/.

sections.title: Comparing ea
paragraphs: Learners often confuse the short vowel with the long vowel. Do not make the vowel too long in every word with these letters. Keep the mouth slightly open and steady instead of stretching your smile. Pay close attention to exceptions where the letters sound like a gliding vowel.
